The laboratory experiments were independent of the course. The experiments we made were about things we hadn't learned yet.

The course in itself is quite substantial. However, I felt that all we did in class lectures were to derive equations and formulae and solve problems in addition to those in the recitation hours. All this can be done using the course book too. What I felt was needed in the class was a deep understanding of concepts, intuition, and methods to think about concepts in general; things that books cannot get across quite effectively. Instead, all focus was put into computations with little attention to ideas in general. The fast-paced derivations and use of formulae made it difficult for me to understand the underlying concepts, even if I could understand the problem-solving techniques. So, I didn't know how to question the concepts when I didn't capture them in the first place.

If the course could be structured to give conceptual understanding, independent of derivations of equations so that we know how to approach any kind of problem, then the learning would be quite effective.
